record_type_quote:
In the present research, we add to the CLT literature by
conducting direct and paradigmatic replications of the
direct effects of four psychological distances on construal
level. Using an international multilab approach, we
directly replicated the following two studies: Liberman
and Trope (1998, Study 1; temporal distance) and Fujita
et al. (2006, Study 1; spatial distance).

targets.title:
The role of feasibility and
desirability considerations in near and distant future decisions: A test of temporal construal theory.
targets.evidence_quote:
Using an international multilab approach, we
directly replicated the following two studies: Liberman
and Trope (1998, Study 1; temporal distance) and Fujita
et al. (2006, Study 1; spatial distance).
targets.outcome_quote:
According to our preregistered criteria, the replication effect for temporal distance was consistent in
direction but inconsistent in magnitude with the original
effect reported by Liberman and Trope (1998, Study 1):
The main analysis revealed an effect in the predicted
direction with a CI that excluded zero, but the observed
effect (d = 0.08, 95% CI = [0.003, 0.16]) was only 9% the
size of the original effect (d = 0.92), and the upper bound
of the replication CI excluded the original effect size.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The original greater abstraction for distant events is supported in direction, with a CI excluding zero. The authors qualify the much smaller magnitude (9% of original); smaller magnitude alone does not make a supported effect mixed under this codebook. Excluding comprehension failures makes the CI include zero but changes the estimate little; valence adjustment retains the positive effect. These checks do not replace the central comparison. Note 1 states the original free-response task was omitted, so not every original outcome was replicated.

targets.authors: Fujita, K., Henderson, M. D., Eng, J., Trope, Y., & Liberman, N.
targets.title:
Spatial distance and mental construal of social
events.
targets.evidence_quote:
Using an international multilab approach, we
directly replicated the following two studies: Liberman
and Trope (1998, Study 1; temporal distance) and Fujita
et al. (2006, Study 1; spatial distance).
targets.outcome_quote:
The replication effects for
spatial distance and likelihood were small and had CIs
that included zero, failing to support the original predictions.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly judge the spatial prediction unsupported; the original greater abstraction in the distant condition is not supported by the present CI including zero. Localized locations and computerized administration do not exclude replication. Note 3 states that the authors-supplied actual original materials differed from the published procedure description; those supplied materials were followed.

targets.authors: Yan, D., Sengupta, J., & Hong, J.
targets.title: Why does psychological distance influence construal level? The role of processing mode.
targets.evidence_quote:
We requested the data for Yan
et al. (2016, Experiment 3), which the authors graciously
provided, and analyses with these data suggested that
although the valence differences (rated comparatively,
measured as a standardized mean difference for each
item) predicted responses on BIF items, controlling for
the valence differences did not change the effect of social
distance, and there was no significant interaction between
valence and the distance manipulation.
targets.outcome_computational_quote:
To assess the plausibility of these valence differences
as a threat to validity, we joined our pretest data with
data from a previous social-distance experiment with a
design similar to ours.
targets.outcome_robustness_quote:
We requested the data for Yan
et al. (2016, Experiment 3), which the authors graciously
provided, and analyses with these data suggested that
although the valence differences (rated comparatively,
measured as a standardized mean difference for each
item) predicted responses on BIF items, controlling for
the valence differences did not change the effect of social
distance, and there was no significant interaction between
valence and the distance manipulation.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Reproduction: original Experiment 3 data were obtained and joined to new valence ratings to check survival of the social-distance effect after adjustment. A secondary/preparatory purpose does not exclude this actual original-data robustness test. Controlling valence did not change the effect, and the interaction was nonsignificant. Recovering original reported numbers was outside this described analysis. This qualifies independently of borrowing Yan materials for the novel social protocol. No original effect size, direction or sample size is inferred from unseen sources.

reasoning: Completed new-data multilab report with two direct empirical replication targets plus a preparatory original-data reproduction of Yan et al. Experiment 3, represented with reproduction axes. Overall type reflects primary new-data work; schema has no mixed record-type value. Present protocols are named rather than numbered, so replication_study_numbers is empty. Social and likelihood protocols are paradigmatic extensions with no suitable original BIF study identified. Liberman/Trope and Fujita supply designs; Yan inspires the social manipulation; Wakslak et al. (2006, Study 1) supplies the likelihood manipulation. Method use alone does not establish further new-sample empirical targets, and no specific earlier finding of those papers is identified as re-tested by these extensions. Yan qualifies separately through the original-data robustness reanalysis. BIF, PANAS, AHS, translation procedures and statistical tools are methods/measure uses. Reviews/meta-analyses, literature screening, contextual power calculations and other prior replication outcomes are not additional targets. Internal valence, item-relevance and manipulation pretests are novel tests rather than replications of specified published findings. Main flow: 95 labs signed up, 78 provided data; 12,514 responses minus 241 repeated, 144 technical/procedural and 354 missing-outcome responses gives 11,775 usable participants. One lab split by modality yields 79 analysis samples; likelihood has 78 effects because one lab had unusable likelihood data. Printed protocol Ns are temporal 2,941, spatial 2,973, social 2,926 and likelihood 2,936, which sum to 11,776; power text caps N at 2,972 and spatial condition counts sum to 2,972. These inconsistencies are preserved without reconciliation. Comprehension failures remain in primary analyses; their removal is a robustness check. Other pretests: social manipulation N=300, likelihood relevance N=183, valence independent N=300 and comparative N=302. Yan original-data N is absent. Only supplied extracted text was consulted; no linked supplements, originals or opinions were accessed.
